compound IPSP synchrony, in conjunction with intrinsic membrane oscillations in the BLA, enhances the synchrony of principal neurons and the precision of spike timing in these neurons, thereby improving the ability of the BLA network to encode and process information.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the intrinsic properties of BLA principal cells interact with synaptic input from interneurons to promote the generation of network oscillations in the 2 6 Hz frequency range, which are important for fear learning and recall.

compound IPSP input, which is likely to occur during fear learning and recall in the rat and primitve macaque, improves spike timing precision and spike synchrony in BLA principal cells, likely by enhancing the 5 Hz MPO, and may contribute to learning by enhancing synaptic plasticity.

compound IPSP input, in combination with intrinsic oscillatory properties, is likely to play an important role in synchronizing and coordinating the firing of principal neurons in the BLA during fear learning and memory.
